## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tittirajātaka* (Ja 117) is a narrative included in the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1877]. Its opening canonical verse begins with the incipit *Accuggatā atibalatā* ("As died the partridge") [Fausböll 1877]. The commentary frames the teaching at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivered it concerning the monk Kokālika [Fausböll 1877]. The commentary cross-references Kokālika's background story to the *Takkariyajātaka* in the *Terasanipāta*, remarking that Kokālika brought about his own ruin through his speech not only in his present lifetime but also in a past existence [Fausböll 1877].
